items.entity: design domain aspect ratio / orientation of the 30×60 element grid
items.description: Fig. 1(a) and Fig. 2 captions only say 'discretized by 30×60 elements'. They do not say which count runs along the cantilever length (horizontal) and which through the height; only the unseen figure shows this. This decides whether the cantilever is long (2:1) or deep (1:2).
readings: 60 elements horizontal (length) × 30 vertical (height): length:height = 2:1
30 elements horizontal × 60 vertical: length:height = 1:2 (deep cantilever)

items.description: No physical lengths or element size are given anywhere, only element counts, and the filter radius is in element units. If elements are square, the absolute size only rescales compliance.
readings: Unit square elements: domain 60×30 (or 30×60) length units
Domain 2×1 (or 1×2) with square elements of size 1/30
Domain 60 mm × 30 mm with 1 mm square elements

items.description: No thickness is given for the 2-D cantilever. Only the 3-D variant in Sec. 3.1 has a thickness (5 elements).
readings: Unit thickness t = 1
t = 1 mm
t equal to one element size

items.entity: downward load at the lower-right corner
items.description: Fig. 1(a) caption: 'a downward distributed load of 1 N is applied at the lower-right corner'. Calling it 'distributed' clashes with a single corner point. The text does not say how many nodes are loaded, which edge(s) the load runs along, or how it is weighted per node; this is shown only in the figure.
readings: Single nodal load at the lower-right corner node (classic top88 cantilever)
Equal nodal forces on the lowest 3 nodes of the right edge (~2 elements, ~7% of height)
Equal nodal forces on the rightmost 3 nodes of the bottom edge
Nodes on both the right and bottom edges around the corner (2–3 on each)
Line load over the lowest ~10% of the right edge with consistent nodal forces (end nodes half weight)

items.entity: '1 N' value of the distributed load
items.description: Fig. 1(a) caption does not say whether 1 N is the total (resultant) load, the force on each loaded node, or a load per unit length.
readings: 1 N resultant split among the loaded nodes
1 N applied at each loaded node
1 N per unit length over the loaded segment

items.description: Fig. 1(a) caption names only the 'design domain (dark gray)'. In Figs. 14 and 17, light-gray shading marks non-design parts. The text never says whether Fig. 1 has a non-design region, e.g. a solid pad at the load point (common in stress problems) or a support block.
readings: No passive elements: whole 30×60 grid is designable
Small solid (rho = 1) non-design patch around the loaded corner nodes (e.g. 2×2 to 3×3 elements)
Shaded block only depicts the clamped wall outside the mesh (no effect on the FE model)

items.entity: Young's modulus of the solid material
items.description: No Young's modulus is given anywhere; the text only says 'linear elasticity' and mentions SIMP in the Introduction.
readings: E0 = 1 (non-dimensional)
E0 = 210 GPa
E0 = 70 GPa

items.description: Poisson's ratio is not specified anywhere in the paper.

items.entity: 2-D constitutive assumption (plane stress vs plane strain)
items.description: The text does not say whether the 2-D cantilever is plane stress or plane strain. This changes the effective Poisson's ratio.
readings: Plane stress
Plane strain

items.description: The Introduction cites SIMP only as common practice. The penalty exponent is never given, and the text never says SIMP is the scheme actually used. The p values in the paper (4, 10, 12, 20) all refer to p-norm stress aggregation.
readings: SIMP, penalty 3 throughout
SIMP with penalty continuation 1 → 3
SIMP, penalty 4

items.description: Sec. 2 gives rho_min = epsilon only as an example ('e.g., epsilon ≈ 1e-6'). It does not say whether stiffness is E0·rho^p with that lower bound or a modified SIMP with a separate Emin.
readings: Design bounds [1e-6, 1] with E = rho^p·E0 (void ≈ 1e-18·E0 for p = 3)
Modified SIMP E = Emin + rho^p (E0 − Emin), Emin = 1e-9·E0 (top88 style)
Lower bound 1e-3 with E = rho^p·E0 (top99 style)

items.entity: MMA move limit eta_max for the Fig. 1 run
items.description: Fig. 1 caption lists the MMA settings but no move limit. eta_max = 0.2 is stated only for Figs. 10(b,c) and 14(b–d). Fig. 3 caption says Fig. 3 differs from Fig. 1 by cutting eta_max to 0.01 after iteration 5, which implies Fig. 1 used a constant but unstated value. Sec. 3.1 also says 'both optimal solutions use the same numerical settings as in Fig. 3', which muddies this.
readings: eta_max = 0.2 constant
eta_max = 0.5 constant
eta_max = 1.0 (no extra move limit beyond MMA asymptotes)
eta_max = 0.2 for 5 iterations, then 0.01 (Fig. 3 schedule)

items.description: Only 'density-filter radius 2.5 (element size)' is given (Fig. 1 caption, Sec. 3.1). The weighting kernel and the treatment at domain edges are not specified.
readings: Linear cone weights max(0, 2.5 − d), normalized, no boundary padding (top88 style)
Same cone filter with padding beyond domain edges
Helmholtz/PDE filter with length scale equivalent to r = 2.5 (r_PDE = 2.5/(2√3))
Gaussian kernel with radius 2.5 elements

items.entity: density field used in stiffness and volume constraint
items.description: Eq. (13) writes K(rho) and the volume constraint using the raw design variables rho. Sec. 3 says the density filter is applied to the design variables during optimization. The text never says whether the volume constraint uses filtered or raw densities.
readings: Filtered (physical) densities in both stiffness and volume constraint
Filtered densities in stiffness, raw design variables in the volume constraint

items.description: Only 'maximum iterations, 100' is given (Fig. 1 caption). No convergence tolerance is stated, so it is unclear whether all 100 iterations are always run.
readings: Always run exactly 100 MMA iterations
Stop early when max |delta rho| < 0.01 (else 100)
Stop early when relative compliance change < 1e-3 (else 100)

items.entity: MMA subproblem parameters and objective scaling
items.description: Sec. 3 and App. A say only that Svanberg's original MMA code is used. The parameters a0, a_i, c_i, d_i, the asymptote settings and any scaling of compliance are not given. With a 100-iteration cap, these affect the optimization path.
readings: a0 = 1, a_i = 0, c_i = 1000, d_i = 0; asyinit 0.5, asyincr 1.2, asydecr 0.7; unscaled compliance
Same, but compliance normalized by its initial value (possibly ×10–100)
